title: Data localization & subprocessor inventory - Northgate Insurance compliance review
customer_attendees: Claire Donovan - Head of Cloud Security
summary: Customer wants explicit EU data residency, ability to pin workloads to region, customer-managed keys, and a full subprocessor map. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options, SSO/RBAC, audit logs retention, and contractual DPA clauses. Agreed next steps: share subprocessor inventory, SOC2/ISO certs, and schedule technical deep dive on BYOK and VPC onboarding.
next_steps: Maya: Send latest subprocessor spreadsheet + DPA template (by 2025-10-10)
Ethan: Schedule 60m technical deep dive on BYOK/VPC with Samir (week of 2025-10-13)
Claire: Share Northgate legal constraints doc and data residency matrix (by 2025-10-09)
action_items: Maya Patel: Attach SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 cert to thread (due 2025-10-09)
Ethan Rios: Produce architecture diagram for Private deployment showing control plane and data plane separation (due 2025-10-14)
Claire Donovan: Provide list of EU regions and regulatory gates where data must remain (due 2025-10-09)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick agenda: region pinning, subprocessor list, KMS options, and a quick Q&A.
[00:10] Claire (Northgate): Thanks, Maya. We primarily need to ensure EU personal data never leaves EU, and we need a subprocessor inventory for our procurement review.
[00:23] Ethan (SE): Great. For clarity, when you say EU-only, do you mean control plane in US but data plane pinned to EU, or fully sovereign control plane as well?
[00:30] Claire: Preferred is data plane pinned to EU and logs stored in EU; control plane can be US if we have contractual assurances, but some of our regulators want a private control plane option.
[00:42] Samir: Also curious about cross-border fallbacks — if EU capacity is saturated do requests route to US? We need guarantees or at least explicit policy.
[00:52] Maya: Understood. Redwood has three modes — hosted, dedicated, private. Hosted by default can be region-affinitized; Dedicated gives reserved EU capacity; Private provides VPC/on-prem with customer-managed networking. For Northgate I'd recommend Dedicated or Private given regulatory posture.
[01:10] Lena (Legal): On subprocessors, we need a running map by country and processing purpose; and an SLA point about not transferring EU-personal-data outside EEA unless an approved mechanism is in place.
[01:22] Ethan: We keep a live subprocessor inventory — I'll attach the spreadsheet. Quick note: some infra subs (CDN, monitoring) may have global control planes but their data residency can be constrained. We'll flag which have cross-border telemetry.
[01:35] Claire: Can you do BYOK? We require tenant keys with key ops restricted to us.
[01:40] Ethan: Yes, BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer a customer-managed KMS integration for encryption-at-rest and envelope encryption, but there are limitations around control plane metadata that still may be in Redwood's control plane for multi-tenant hosted.
[01:55] Maya: Important to call out: BYOK for Hosted still involves some metadata and logs that we must keep for platform health; we can limit retention and provide audit logs showing access, but total control is stronger in Private.
[02:06] Samir: What about audit log retention and export? We need immutable audit trails for three years and ability to push logs to our SIEM.
[02:13] Ethan: We stream audit logs to customer destinations in Dedicated/Private via secured syslog or S3 with server-side encryption. Retention policies are configurable and we can provide signed attestations.
[02:25] Claire: Any SOC 2 or ISO proof we can share? Procurement needs artifacts.
[02:29] Maya: We'll send SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates after an NDA — I'll include those in the follow-up.
[02:36] Speaker 3: (inaudible) — service map?
[02:40] Ethan: Also worth noting subprocessor categories: compute, storage, telemetry, identity, and networking. For each we provide country, subprocess type, and whether they can see PII.
[02:54] Claire: For identity, we need SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning — can Redwood integrate with our Okta?
[03:00] Maya: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM are supported across Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports SAML but SCIM for user provisioning is enterprise plan.
[03:13] Samir: RBAC granularity? We need least-privilege across teams and an admin audit trail.
[03:17] Ethan: RBAC supports roles: org-admin, project-admin, developer, viewer. All admin actions are logged; we can export role-assignment histories for audits.
[03:28] Claire: How do you handle data deletion/erasure requests? We have to demonstrate timely deletion and proof for regulators.
[03:34] Ethan: We support data lifecycle policies: at-rest object deletion and KV cache eviction. For Hosted, some logs remain for retention period — we can shorten retention for Northgate as part of the contract and provide deletion certificates or attestations.
[03:50] Lena: Is there any chance telemetry or support access could expose plaintext data? We need to understand support tooling access and safeguards.
[03:58] Maya: Support access is role-gated and audited. For Private, support access requires explicit customer enablement. We use session recordings for support ops but PII is redacted where possible; for high-sensitivity customers we can run support sessions in customer VPC.
[04:14] Claire: For region pinning — how do you enforce at routing layer? Is it best-effort or contractual?
[04:21] Ethan: We have policy-based routing: requests are matched to region by customer config; for Dedicated/Private you can pin to a region and requests are routed to capacity in that region only. For Hosted we offer region-affinity with fallback options; we can write a strict no-fallback policy as a contractual SLO for EU-only processing but that implies queueing or 429s if capacity exhausted.
[04:46] Samir: So if we require strict EU-only processing, what happens during spikes? Do requests fail?
[04:52] Ethan: Either queueing/backpressure or 429/500 — or we can contract reserved capacity (Dedicated) to avoid that. There's a cost tradeoff.
[05:02] Claire: We need the subprocessor list to feed legal procurement. Can you enumerate which third parties handle content vs metadata?
[05:11] Ethan: Yes. We'll mark each subprocessor as content processor, metadata/telemetry, or control plane only. Some CDNs may see request headers but not stored content.
[05:20] Lena: About contractual clauses: we need standard DPA with SCCs or equivalent, and audit rights. Is that included?
[05:27] Maya: Yes, DPA with SCCs available; audit rights can be scoped — for Private we offer more expansive audit options including on-prem inspection or joint audits.
[05:37] Claire: Encryption in transit — TLS, mutual TLS for streams?
[05:41] Ethan: TLS 1.2+ for all in-transit. For customer destinations we support mTLS and IP allowlisting for log sinks.
[05:49] Samir: Curious about metadata replication — do model KV caches replicate across regions? Could that leak data across borders?
[05:56] Ethan: Good question. KV caches for inference are scoped to the serving cluster and do not replicate across regions unless you enable cross-region failover. For Dedicated/Private we can disable cross-region replication.
[06:12] Claire: Are there any subprocessors in Russia/China? Our policy forbids them.
[06:18] Maya: We don't use subprocessors based in sanctioned jurisdictions for processing EEA personal data—we'll flag any exceptions in the spreadsheet.
[06:28] Lena: Will you provide a signed attestation for that?
[06:31] Maya: Yes, we can provide a signed statement as part of procurement.
[06:36] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[06:40] Ethan: One operational note: export controls — certain models may be restricted by export jurisdiction, we'll call that out during model selection.
[06:50] Samir: For BYOK, can we rotate keys without service interruption?
[06:55] Ethan: Key rotation is supported with grace windows; for Dedicated/Private you can rotate with minimal interruption. Hosted has rolling rewraps; we'll detail the process in the deep dive.
[07:08] Claire: Regarding logs, do you provide immutable WORM storage or are logs mutable?
[07:14] Ethan: We can push to S3 with object lock for WORM-style retention in Dedicated/Private. Hosted options depend on provider but we can deliver export to customer-owned buckets.
[07:26] Lena: This is great. Procurement will need the subprocessor map and a listing of where each processor's control plane is located.
[07:35] Maya: We'll provide a per-subprocessor matrix with country, processing purpose, whether PII is accessible, and contact details.
[07:44] Claire: Can we have a short escalation path for incident response? Typical SLA timelines: 2 hours for severity 1 notification.
[07:51] Ethan: Our incident response runbook includes initial notification within 2 hours for Sev1, and full RCA within 30 days; we can adapt to Northgate's requirements contractually.
[08:04] Samir: Any concerns about slowdowns when using Dedicated EU-only — do you have perf numbers?
[08:10] Ethan: We have benchmarks for EU regions; Dedicated gives predictable p95 latency due to reserved GPU pools. We'll share a latency/throughput spreadsheet for your app profile.
[08:22] Claire: For legal, if there's a lawful request from a non-EEA court can you notify us and contest requests?
[08:28] Lena: We need notification clauses and mutual defense steps.
[08:31] Maya: We notify customers of legal process affecting customer data unless prohibited; for Private we run through customer's legal counsel. We'll add standard notification language to the DPA.
[08:43] Claire: Ok, last set of items: timeline. We aim to select a vendor by end of October and pilot in November. Can Redwood meet a POC in November?
[08:52] Maya: Yes — if we have approvals, a Dedicated pilot or Private proof-of-concept is doable in November. We'll need the signed DPA and technical contacts to provision.
[09:00] Ethan: Action: I'll produce the subprocessor sheet and flag cross-border items and KMS options.
[09:06] Maya: I'll assemble SOC2 docs and DPA.
[09:09] Claire: We'll send the procurement matrix and region list.
[09:12] Speaker 1: Thanks everyone.
[09:16] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send subprocessor inventory, SOC2/ISO certs, DPA template; schedule BYOK/VPC technical deep dive.
[09:25] Claire: Thanks, speak soon.
[09:28] [call end] Note: transcription contains autocaption inaccuracies; proper nouns sometimes garbled (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache).
notes: References: link to security deck (internal): https://redwood.example.com/security/attachments/northgate-2025-q4; subprocessor spreadsheet will be shared as an attachment in follow-up email.
closing: Call ended with clear next steps; procurement timeline aligns with vendor selection by end-Oct.
